title: Playtesting
summary: Find three improvements that would make FX Crossroads clearer, fairer or more enjoyable.
body: Choose areas to test: controls, menus, mobile interaction, combat, progression, multiplayer or performance. Record your device, hero, mode and the exact steps. Separate bugs from design suggestions. Repeat a problem to see whether it is consistent.
task: For each of three findings, explain the problem, who it affects, your proposed change and how you would verify the fix.
deliver: A test report listing what you tested and how, three evidence-backed improvements, and a reflection on your process. Include screenshots or short clips where useful. Studio test reports can support your evidence.
criteria: Can someone else reproduce your finding? Is your solution practical? Did you explain what worked well too?

title: Heroes & enemies
summary: Design a new character that adds a useful role and belongs in the Crossroads world.
body: Create four poses, attacks and readable counterplay in Hero Workshop or Enemy Lab. Alternate Forms can change appearance during an ability. Finalize your project, then playtest it; a Student submission freezes the art and values for review.
task: Choose a gap in the roster. Create a rough concept, get peer feedback, then build and test one distinctive mechanic.
deliver: Finalized hero or enemy JSON, original artwork and a short test report. Add brief intent, one revision and credits.
criteria: Readable at game size; attacks match their graphics; strengths have limits; lore fits the world.

title: Behaviour redesign
summary: Improve how a character or enemy behaves without losing its identity.
body: Use Behaviour Lab to change movement and decisions. Keep the same enemy art and attacks while testing different code, so your comparison isolates the behaviour.
task: Pick one frustrating or repetitive behaviour. Sketch the decisions, prototype the supported parts, and compare before and after.
deliver: A behaviour diagram or pseudocode, prototype or proposed code changes, and a comparison report with evidence.
criteria: Predictable enough to learn, varied enough to stay interesting, and fair to different hero roles.

title: Realm design
summary: Make a place worth exploring, with a clear route and memorable encounters.
body: Use Object & Raster Lab to make props, then Realm Builder to paint terrain and place objects and enemies. Set movement/projectile blocking separately. Record a vision first, check that spawn and exit connect, and Finalize & Play to test the route.
task: Redesign an existing realm section or plan a new one. Walk a partner through the map and ask where they would go next.
deliver: Portable realm JSON, at least three matching props, a short vision and test summary. Optional screenshots show before/after routes.
criteria: Clear navigation, reliable collision, readable hazards, balanced pacing and sensible performance.

title: Tutorial & promotion
summary: Help a new player understand the game, or make them curious enough to try it.
body: A tutorial teaches one task at a time. A promotional video shows a strong hook and the game’s identity. Plan audience, script, shot list, captions, audio and length. Use spectator views for clear action footage. Label staged GameDev footage when relevant.
task: Storyboard a short tutorial or trailer. Test it with someone who has not played: what did they learn or want to try?
deliver: Storyboard and script, finished video, and a reflection on editing choices and audience feedback.
criteria: Readable captions, clear sound, accurate claims, focused pacing and a purposeful call to action.

title: Music & sound
summary: Give a location or action its own sound while keeping play information clear.
body: Choose a mood and purpose. Music should loop cleanly; sound effects should tell players about attacks, danger, healing or success. Leave space for important cues. Use original or appropriately licensed material and record credits.
task: Create a short looping background track or a small set of related effects. Compare it at normal and quiet volume during play.
deliver: Audio files, a cue sheet explaining where each sound belongs, licence or authorship details, and listening-test feedback.
criteria: Clean loop points, balanced volume, clear cues, no clipping and a style that fits FX Crossroads.
